cards.title: Top of the Ladder
cards.instruction: Carry yourself as the highest-status person present. Treat questions as requests for your approval.

cards.title: Raise the Impossibility
cards.instruction: Answer every strange offer with a more committed version that you can still justify.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I'll decide how we handle this. Your invisible guest is welcome at our wedding. I'll reserve places for invisible companions.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Her family can walk through walls. They tend to wander.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: You can question the details after my decision. I'll rent a ballroom that follows them. Nobody should miss cake.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Our ballroom can split itself when guests wander apart.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then I'll order a cake that multiplies with it. Every room deserves the first slice.

cardFidelity.evidence: A1 reserves wedding places and A3 rents a room; these are generous escalations, but the status prefaces do little to change the hospitality tactic.

responseLogic.evidence: B2 wandering relatives causes A3 following ballroom; B4 splitting ballroom causes A5 multiplying cake with an explicit first-slice rationale.

relationship.evidence: B2 and B4 contribute relevant guest behavior and venue capacity; A3 labels information questioning without a demonstrated challenge.

heightening.evidence: A5 gives each B4 split room its own first slice, extending hospitality through the supplied impossible solution.

specificity.evidence: A1 wedding and B2 guest family establish sufficient roles; no guest biology or rental history is required.

brevityWit.evidence: A3 generic questioning preface interrupts the helpful information chain; A5 cake is earned by B4 splitting.
